summary: Crawlee is a mature, production-grade web scraping and browser automation library for Node.js/TypeScript built by Apify. It provides a unified interface for both HTTP-based crawling (Cheerio, JSDOM, LinkeDOM parsers) and real-browser crawling (Playwright, Puppeteer, Stagehand). The architecture is a Yarn monorepo with ~20 packages, where @crawlee/core provides Request/RequestQueue/RequestList/Dataset/KeyValueStore storage primitives, @crawlee/basic-crawler provides the foundational BasicCrawler with autoscaling, retry logic, session management, and proxy rotation, and specialized crawlers extend this for HTTP vs browser-based scraping. The library is battle-tested on the Apify platform with extensive features: persistent queues, automatic scaling via AutoscaledPool, integrated proxy rotation with session management, fingerprint generation/injection for anti-bot evasion, robots.txt compliance, configurable routing via Router, and comprehensive error handling with retries. Code quality is high with strict TypeScript, comprehensive tests (5000+ commits, 90+ contributors), and active maintenance (last commit Aug 2026).

findings.description:
- Unified crawler interface: single API for HTTP (Cheerio/JSDOM/LinkeDOM) and browser (Playwright/Puppeteer/Stagehand) crawling
- Request management: RequestQueue (dynamic, persistent), RequestList (static), RequestManagerTandem (combined)
- Storage: Dataset (tabular), KeyValueStore (files/state), automatic persistence
- Autoscaling: AutoscaledPool with CPU/memory awareness, configurable min/max concurrency, max requests/minute
- Session & proxy: SessionPool with rotation, ProxyConfiguration with tiered proxies, automatic cookie persistence per session
- Anti-bot: Fingerprint generation/injection (fingerprint-generator + fingerprint-injector), browser-like TLS fingerprints, human-like headers, Cloudflare/Google challenge handling
- Lifecycle hooks: pre/post navigation, pre/post page create/close, request/response hooks
- Routing: Router with label-based handlers, schema validation for userData
- Robots.txt: Automatic fetching/caching, configurable user-agent
- Error handling: Retry logic with maxRetries, session rotation separate from retries, critical/non-retryable errors, error tracking with snapshots
- Export: JSON/CSV dataset export, streaming downloads
- Docker-ready templates, CLI for project scaffolding

integrationPoints:
- **Playwright integration**: Native PlaywrightCrawler uses Playwright directly; BrowserPool manages Playwright browsers with incognito contexts
- **Queue system**: RequestQueue (persistent, SQLite-backed) integrates with any crawler; supports priority, reclaim, lock semantics
- **Search/matching**: Router provides label-based routing; enqueueLinks supports glob/regex filtering with transformRequestFunction for URL normalization; Dataset allows querying exported data
- **Pipeline integration**: 
  - `crawler.run()` returns FinalStatistics for monitoring
  - `crawler.pushData()` / `Dataset.pushData()` for ETL output
  - `crawler.useState()` for persistent crawler state across runs
  - Event system (EventType.PERSIST_STATE, MIGRATING, ABORTING) for graceful shutdown
  - `crawler.addRequests()` for dynamic URL injection during crawl
  - Export to JSON/CSV for downstream processing
- **Proxy/Session**: ProxyConfiguration integrates with Apify Proxy or custom proxies; SessionPool ties sessions to fingerprints for consistency
strengthsForVeridian:
- Battle-tested at scale on Apify platform (millions of pages)
- Excellent anti-bot evasion out of the box (fingerprints, TLS, headers, challenge handling)
- Unified API lets you swap HTTP vs browser crawling with minimal code changes
- Built-in persistence (RequestQueue, Dataset) survives restarts/migrations
- Autoscaling prevents OOM/CPU exhaustion on laptop specs pages
- TypeScript-first with excellent generics for type-safe scraping
- Router + schema validation enables maintainable multi-page-type scrapers
- Session + fingerprint cache makes repeated visits look like real users
- Active maintenance, comprehensive docs, large community
weaknessesForVeridian:
- Heavy dependency tree (Playwright + Puppeteer + fingerprint libs + got-scraping + many utils)
- BrowserPool adds complexity; may be overkill for simple HTTP-only scraping
- Apify-centric defaults (storage paths, proxy integration, event system)
- Learning curve: many options, hooks, and extension points
- No built-in sitemap discovery (utils exist but not integrated into crawler)
- Memory storage is in-memory only (not for production)
- Some APIs still in flux (experiments, CrawlerExtension)
- Bundle size significant if importing full `crawlee` meta-package
